title: Persian Ironwood: Ancient Ironwoods You Can Visit
meta_description: A witch hazel relative from the Caspian forests. Vienna's, on Schmerlingplatz, is 460 cm round at the base and twice as wide as it is tall.
intro: The Persian ironwood is a relative of the witch hazel from the forests south of the Caspian Sea, named for its hard wood and planted for its bark and its autumn colour. It tends to grow out rather than up. Vienna's on Schmerlingplatz is 460 centimetres round at the base and twice as wide as it is tall, and the city protected it in 1956 for its rarity alone. In Leiden, three low spreading ironwoods in Het Plantsoen, planted between 1910 and 1920, gave their name to a cultivar nurseries across Europe still sell. Frankfurt's on the Untermainkai, multi-stemmed and protected in groups, are the tall exception at 19 to 23 metres. In Queens, a slim one in Kissena Park has been on New York's Great Trees list since the first, in 1985. Biltmore in Asheville once called its ironwood a champion, and published no size.
